headline: High risk: Devin’s autonomous cloud workspace and kotaemon’s document/API ingestion create default-path data leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, and shared integrations, while kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, chat transcripts, and citations. If Devin forwards kotaemon-produced content into an instruction-following workflow, prompt-like text can be misread. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Devin imports kotaemon output into an MCP or browser workflow without provenance tagging
IF kotaemon processes attacker-controlled HTML or chat transcripts that Devin later reuses as instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all kotaemon outputs before Devin consumes them
Disable automatic reuse of retrieved text as instructions
Review one sample end-to-end prompt chain for instruction leakage
Restrict Devin to read-only ingestion from kotaemon outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo clones, cloud workspace files, secrets, and broad network egress; kotaemon processes documents and API keys and can send content to external LLM APIs. In a shared workflow, sensitive files or transcripts can flow from Devin into kotaemon’s inference path or from kotaemon into Devin’s workspace, creating default-path leakage with third-party exposure.
conditions: IF Devin places secrets or private repo files into kotaemon indexes or chats
IF kotaemon routes uploaded documents or API keys to a hosted model backend
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders and uploads
Use a local-only model backend for kotaemon
Separate Devin and kotaemon workspaces at the OS level
Rotate any API keys that were exposed to either system
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write files, modify git state, and use broad cloud workspace shell access; kotaemon writes to ./ktem_app_data and handles API keys. If both touch the same repository or mounted directory, concurrent writes can overwrite artifacts or corrupt state. The conflict is plausible from the profiles, though not directly documented as a shared directory.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout or shared volume
IF kotaemon persists state in a directory Devin also edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared files
Use git branches with explicit merge review
Back up the shared directory before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is autonomous and can act on browser, shell, and integration outputs; kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that surfaces documents, citations, and chat transcripts. If Devin treats kotaemon’s retrieved text as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly observed, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Devin uses kotaemon outputs as source material for commits or external messages
IF kotaemon returns stale or hallucinated citations that Devin does not verify
mitigations: Require human review before Devin acts on kotaemon outputs
Cross-check citations against source documents
Limit Devin to drafting, not sending, downstream actions
Mark kotaemon outputs as untrusted in the workflow
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action execution

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches team chat, issue trackers, docs, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace; kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys with configurable external model backends. If regulated or confidential content is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF EU personal data or PHI is uploaded into kotaemon while Devin stores it in a cloud workspace
IF retention or deletion policies differ between Devin integrations and kotaemon backends
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Keep regulated data out of external model backends
Document retention settings for both systems
Delete any duplicated sensitive artifacts after use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
